THO-01.name: Foundation & reinforced concrete
THO-01.method: Excavate footings, fabricate rebar, pour concrete per structural drawings.
THO-01.note: Applies to load-bearing foundation, columns, beams, and slabs.

THO-02.name: Masonry walls
THO-02.material: Tuynel bricks with M75 cement mortar.
THO-02.method: Build 100–200 mm walls, plaster both sides plumb.
THO-02.note: Includes both partition and external perimeter walls.

THO-03.name: Waterproofing
THO-03.method: Two coats on bathroom floors, roof deck and adjoining walls.

THO-04.name: Embedded electrical & plumbing
THO-04.material: Binh Minh PVC conduit, Cadivi 2×2.5 mm² wire.
THO-04.method: Run conduits inside walls and slabs before pouring concrete.
THO-04.note: Includes Internet and camera signal lines.

THO-05.name: Concrete staircase
THO-05.method: Pour staircase monolithically, grind tread surfaces.
THO-05.note: Treads prepared for stone cladding in the finishing stage.

THO-TUM.name: Rooftop tum (stair enclosure)
THO-TUM.method: Build enclosing walls + pour RC roof over the rooftop stair.
THO-TUM.note: Shown only when the project has tum enabled.

THO-ST.name: Terrace parapet / railing
THO-ST.material: RC + plastered brick, or stainless-steel railing.
THO-ST.method: Build a 900 mm perimeter wall, waterproof the base fillet.
THO-ST.note: Shown only when the project has an open (unroofed) terrace.

HT-01.name: Floor & wall tiling
HT-01.material: Basic: 60×60 ceramic. Standard: Dong Tam granite. Premium: natural marble.
HT-01.method: Tile every floor, tile bathroom & kitchen walls.

HT-02.name: Wall paint

HT-02.method: 1 primer + 2 top coats, with crack-resistant putty prep.

HT-03.name: Plasterboard ceiling
HT-03.material: Basic: Vinh Tuong frame, 9 mm board. Standard: moisture-proof board. Premium: tray ceiling + cove lighting.

HT-04.name: Doors & windows
HT-04.material: Basic: Xingfa aluminium. Standard: PMI aluminium + Low-E glass. Premium: solid wood + acoustic glass.
HT-04.method: Fabricate at the workshop, install and finish on site.

HT-05.name: Sanitary ware
HT-05.material: Basic: Inax basic. Standard: American Standard. Premium: Toto / Kohler.
HT-05.method: Install toilet, basin, shower and matching accessories.

HT-06.name: Electrical devices & lighting

NT-01.note: Includes stone benchtop and stainless-steel sink.

ctas.pdfComingSoon: PDF export is coming in the next release.

tooltips.chip: A townhouse supports up to 1 ground + 4 upper floors + 1 special floor (tum and/or terrace). The config is inherited from the project-creation step.
tooltips.marketShares: These are average market cost shares — only a rough reference. The donut below reflects the real numbers for your project; the two can differ.
tooltips.tum: The tum is a small enclosure over the rooftop stairwell. The terrace is an open rooftop (for drying laundry, relaxing). The owner picks these when creating the project.

area.land: Total plot area, taken from the title deed or drawing.
area.groundFloor: The actually-built ground-floor footprint — usually smaller than the plot because of front/back yards and pathways.
area.totalFloor: Sum of the floor area of every level (ground + upper floors + tum). Used to price rough and finishing.
area.usable: Livable area = total floor × {factor, number, ::percent}. Townhouses lose ~20% to stairs, walls, service shafts (apartments are higher because they don't need private stairs). Interior is priced against this number.
area.floorCount: Counted as 1 ground + 4 upper floors = 5, plus any tum. The tum is treated as an auxiliary floor, so it's listed separately.
area.height: Estimated as number of floors × ~3.2 m + tum height. Just an estimate, not the surveyed height.

tooltips.packageHeader: The package sets the finishing and interior material grade — the higher, the pricier per m². Switching packages recomputes those two portions.
tooltips.roughLocked: Rough is the structural skeleton (foundation, columns, beams, slabs, walls). It's tied to the structure, not to the fanciness of the interior — so its price stays the same at every tier. Finishing is priced over the total floor (all tiling and paint); interior is priced over the usable area (furniture only lives in real usable space).
tooltips.unit: Quantity unit: m² (area), m³ (volume), m (linear metre — for things measured by length like railings), set (a bundled scope like a staircase).
tooltips.btct: BTCT = reinforced concrete. Covers foundations, columns, beams and slabs — the frame that carries all the home's load.
tooltips.md: m (linear) = linear metre. The railing runs along the terrace edge, so it's measured by length rather than area. Only applies if a terrace is chosen.
tooltips.dk: Cond = conditional line item: it only appears when the project has tum / terrace enabled in the creation step.
tooltips.progressTarget: The target is the expected spend for this portion alone. The bar shows how much of it is used — over 100% turns red as a warning.
tooltips.donut: The percentages come from the real numbers for the three portions in the table — this reflects your project directly, unlike the market averages in the consultation copy at the top.

privacy.intro: This policy explains how we collect, use and protect your personal data in accordance with Vietnam's Decree 13/2023/ND-CP on personal data protection.

sections.title: 1. Data we collect
sections.body: Account details (name, email, phone), floor-plan images you upload for AI processing, and contact/lead form submissions. We do not collect land-title (deed) documents.

sections.title: 2. How we use data
sections.body: To provide the design and estimate services, respond to your requests, and improve the platform.

sections.title: 3. Image data

sections.title: 4. Data sharing
